sources.claim_as_shown: 76 out of 100 people who search on their phone for something nearby visit a business within a day.
sources.title: How Mobile Search Connects Consumers to Stores
sources.notes: One-page Google PDF, downloaded and read in full. Exact text: '76% of people who search on their smartphones for something nearby visit a business within a day' and '28% of those searches for something nearby result in a purchase'. Footnote 7: 'Google/Purchased Digital Diary: How Consumers Solve Their Needs in the Moment, May 2016. Smartphone users = 1000, local searchers = 634, purchases = 1,140.' US study. No Indian equivalent found on a page we could open, so the slide must say 'US study, 2016'. The old Think with Google article page for this figure now redirects to business.google.com/in/think, so cite the PDF only.

sources.claim_as_shown: Customers are 2.7 times more likely to consider a business reputable if they find a complete Business Profile on Google Search and Maps.
sources.title: Complete your Business Profile on Google
sources.notes: Opened and read. Exact text: 'Customers are 2.7 times more likely to consider a business reputable if they find a complete Business Profile on Google Search and Maps. Customers are 70% more likely to visit and 50% more likely to consider purchasing from businesses with a complete Business Profile.' Google gives no year or study name on the page; show it as 'Google Business Profile Help, page read 2026'. Page returns 404 to a HEAD request but 200 to GET, so the link checker should use GET. The same page lists what a complete profile needs: services, photos and videos, description, opening date, business hours, reviews link, attributes. Use that list for the interactive checklist.

sources.claim_as_shown: Customers are 70% more likely to visit, and 50% more likely to consider buying from, a business with a complete Google profile.
sources.title: Complete your Business Profile on Google
sources.notes: Same page and sentence as s02-02. Google's own claim, no independent study named.

sources.claim_as_shown: Every month Google connects people to nearby businesses more than 9 billion times, including over 1 billion phone calls and 3 billion requests for directions.
sources.title: Say hello to the new Google My Business app, and say hello to your next customer
sources.notes: Opened and read. Post dated 14 November 2018 by Curtis Galloway, Engineering Manager, Google My Business. Exact text: 'Every month, Google connects people to businesses nearby more than 9 billion times, including over 1 billion phone calls and 3 billion direction requests to stores.' Global figure; say so on the slide.

sources.claim_as_shown: 'Near me' searches in India grew 75% in a year.
sources.title: Year in Search, India: Insights for Brands
sources.notes: 97-page Google PDF, downloaded and read. Page 11: '75% YoY growth in "near me" queries'. Source line on that page: 'Google Internal Data, January - December, 2018'. PDF created May 2019. Indian figure. Same report, page 22: '400% growth for "dealer near me" searches' (Google Internal Data, January to November 2018), usable as a second Indian example if needed.

sources.claim_as_shown: 68 out of 100 Indian small and medium businesses were completely offline, and only 2 in 100 actively sold or promoted online.
sources.title: Impact of internet and digitisation on SMBs in India
sources.notes: 29-page PDF, downloaded and read. Exact text: 'A staggering 68 per cent of Indian SMBs are completely offline, with only 2 per cent actively selling or promoting their business online.' Based on a Kantar IMRB telephone survey of 504 Indian SMBs in November 2016. Indian figure, but nine years old; label the year clearly. URL 301-redirects to assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/in/pdf/2017/01/Impact-of-internet-and-digitisation.pdf, which returns 200.

sources.claim_as_shown: Indian small businesses that use digital tools grow revenues and profits up to twice as fast as those that stay offline.
sources.title: Impact of internet and digitisation on SMBs in India
sources.notes: Same PDF as s02-06. Page 15 heading: 'Digital SMBs grow revenues and profits up to twice as fast as Offline counterparts'. Summary page: 'Grow profits up to two times faster than Offline SMBs'. Say 'up to' on the slide.

sources.claim_as_shown: 89 out of 100 consumers expect business owners to reply to reviews.
sources.title: Local Consumer Review Survey 2026
sources.notes: Opened and read. Survey of 1,002 US adult consumers via SurveyMonkey, published 11 February 2026. Page states '89% expect owners to respond' and '80% are likely to use a business that responds to all reviews'. US sample; no Indian equivalent found, so say 'US survey' on the slide.

sources.claim_as_shown: 74 out of 100 consumers only pay attention to reviews written in the last three months.
sources.title: Local Consumer Review Survey 2026
sources.notes: Same page as s02-08. Page states '74% only care about reviews from the last three months' and '44% say the review must be from the last month'. This is the fact behind Sharma's 'two reviews from 2021' before state. US sample, 2026.

sources.claim_as_shown: 47 out of 100 consumers will not use a business that has fewer than 20 reviews.
sources.title: Local Consumer Review Survey 2026
sources.notes: Same page as s02-08. Page states '47% won't use a business with fewer than 20 reviews'. Supports the Sharma after state of 40 reviews. US sample, 2026.

sources.claim_as_shown: More than 200 million businesses a month use the WhatsApp Business app worldwide.
sources.title: Second Quarter 2023 Results Conference Call transcript
sources.notes: 19-page PDF from Meta's investor relations site, downloaded and read. Call dated 26 July 2023. Mark Zuckerberg: 'the 200 million users of our WhatsApp Business app will now be able to create Click-to-WhatsApp ads'. Susan Li: 'the WhatsApp Business App, which now has more than 200 million monthly users.' Global figure; Meta does not publish an India-only number for the app (see notes_unverified).

recommended_use.guess_the_number: s02-01 (76% visit within a day). Poll: 'Of 100 people who search on their phone for something nearby, how many visit a business within a day?' Options 25 / 50 / 76 / 90. Reveal 76. Alternative if a less dated number is preferred: s02-02 (2.7 times), poll 'How many times more likely is a customer to see a business as reputable when its Google profile is complete?' Options 1.2 / 1.8 / 2.7 / 5.
recommended_use.midway_facts: s02-02 and s02-03 on the Google profile standard slide; s02-04 on the 'home is Google, not the website' point; s02-05 and s02-06 as the Indian context pair; s02-08, s02-09, s02-10 on the Sharma before and after reviews slide; s02-11 on the WhatsApp Business slide.

notes_unverified: Share of clicks that go to the top three Google Maps results (the '44%' figure): widely repeated but every page traced it to a single small Neil Patel click study or to unnamed WebFX, BrightLocal or Backlinko data, with competing values of 30%, 42% and 44%. No primary page opened confirms it. Dropped; s02-01 is used for the guess-the-number instead.

WhatsApp Business app users in India ('more than 15 million', 2020): the WhatsApp blog post 'WhatsApp Business app now delivering for 50 million businesses' is rendered by JavaScript and returned only navigation text to WebFetch, curl and a headless Chrome DOM dump, so the figure could not be read on the page. Meta India has said publicly it does not break out the India number. Dropped.

India internet users 2025 (IAMAI-Kantar 'Internet in India 2025', about 958 million): only press coverage found; the IAMAI site still lists the 2024 PDF (886 million users in 2024). Not needed for this session; Session 1 owns this figure.

Think with Google India 'What is India searching for' (2020) near-me growth rows (pharmacy near me +58%, grocery delivery near me +550%, vet doctor near me +60%) were confirmed in the PDF but are COVID-period categories, so they were left out as not relevant to a plumbing audience.
Google India SMB counts (23 million SMBs reached, 2019; 26 million listings, 2017) exist only in press reports of executive quotes, not on a Google page. Dropped.
The old Think with Google article page for the 76% statistic (thinkwithgoogle.com/data/mobile-near-me-searches) now 301-redirects to business.google.com/in/think, so the PDF is cited instead.
